title: Malware types (viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware)
prompt_md:
# Coding problem, 4.1.a: Classify malware by behavioral signature

**Skill:** Analyze Risk · **Maps to:** 4.1.A, 4.1.B · **Language:** Python 3 (pytest)

## Problem
A security analyst receives short incident-report strings that describe observed device behavior.
Build the classifier that maps each description to the correct malware category.

Categories:
- `"virus"`, attaches to host files; spreads when files are shared or opened
- `"worm"`, self-propagates across the network without user action; autonomous scanning
- `"trojan"`, disguised as legitimate software; creates backdoor / exfiltrates data
- `"ransomware"`, encrypts files; demands payment for decryption key

A report may match exactly one category. If no category matches, return `"unknown"`.

## Function contract
Implement `solve(report: str) -> str` in the code editor (see the Reference section below).
Return the single category label string. Matching is case-insensitive substring detection using
the indicator sets defined in the Reference section below.

## Input
A single string describing observed behavior on a device or network.

## Output
One of: `"virus"`, `"worm"`, `"trojan"`, `"ransomware"`, `"unknown"`.

## Examples
```
"Device is scanning all ports on the subnet with no user logged in" -> "worm"
"All .docx files have been encrypted; a ransom note appeared on the desktop" -> "ransomware"
"A free game installer is sending keystrokes to a remote server" -> "trojan"
"An email attachment infected the file and spread copies to shared folders" -> "virus"
"Battery usage is higher than usual after a long meeting" -> "unknown"
```

## Constraints
- Deterministic, offline, standard library only.
- Detection by case-insensitive substring match against indicator sets in the Reference section below.
- Exactly one label returned (string, not list).
- Must pass all cases in the tests (visible + hidden).

interface_md:
# Interface, 4.1.a-malware-classifier (blackbox contract, human-readable)

Any implementation that satisfies this interface can be swapped in (reference, student, or
composite) and must pass the tests unchanged.

## Entry point
```python
def solve(report: str) -> str
```

## Input (`report`)
A single string describing observed device or network behavior.

## Output (`result`)
Exactly one string from `{"virus", "worm", "trojan", "ransomware", "unknown"}`.

## Indicator phrase sets (case-insensitive substring match)
- **worm:** `scanning`, `self-propagat`, `autonomous`, `no user action`, `spreading across network`,
  `network scan`, `subnet scan`, `port scan`, `exploiting vulnerab`
- **ransomware:** `encrypt`, `ransom`, `decryption key`, `locked`, `.locked`, `bitcoin`, `btc`,
  `pay to recover`, `files inaccessible`
- **trojan:** `backdoor`, `keylog`, `exfiltrat`, `disguised`, `fake installer`, `remote control`,
  `command and control`, `c2`, `sending keystrokes`, `free crack`, `pirated`
- **virus:** `host file`, `infected file`, `macro`, `attachment infected`, `spread copies`,
  `shared folder infect`, `email attachment`, `copied to usb`, `file infect`
- If no indicator matches: return `"unknown"`.
- Priority order when multiple sets match (should not occur in well-formed test data, but if it
  does): worm > ransomware > trojan > virus > unknown.

## Guarantees / rules
- Pure function, deterministic, no I/O, no network. Standard library only.
- Matching is case-insensitive substring match.
- Returns a single string (not a list).

## Acceptance
Your code passes when every test below shows a checkmark (some are hidden until you run them).
